parsed.study_design: Case study using informant interviews and field observations
parsed.population_and_sample: Rural households and farmers in semi-arid areas of Gansu Province; no formal sample size reported. Informants included local officials, academics, and rural residents.
parsed.exposure: Implementation and targeting of the government-sponsored 1-2-1 rainwater-harvesting programme, including public provision of concrete and household contributions of labour and sand.
parsed.outcome: Household drinking-water availability and exclusion from access; reported effects included reduced water hauling, improved hygiene, and continued inadequate access among poor, labour-constrained, remote, or programme-excluded households.
parsed.rationale: The introduction and brief history sections (pp. 76–77) identify this as a case study of a provincial government programme that reportedly addressed household drinking-water shortages for over one million rural residents. The “Sources of the project’s success” section (p. 78) draws on academic and rural informants and reports access barriers tied to programme eligibility, remoteness, labour, and inability to afford sand, while Note 2 documents an interview with Gansu Water Conservancy Bureau officials. Although methods and sampling are sparsely reported, the population, administrative exposure, access outcomes, and qualitative case-study design are identifiable.
